context:
Goal: every repo's CLAUDE.md holds only what each session there needs, with no fixed number you have to defend.
Problem (rule): lint/check_claude_md_size.py warns past a copied 200 lines. Lines are the wrong unit: our own CLAUDE.md is 108 lines but 25,354 bytes, because 19 lines run past 300 characters; banchi is 411 lines at about 37.8 KB. A file passes by writing longer lines.
Based on (read): Claude Code's memory docs today (read 19:24 CST): "target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence." So the number is current, not stale; it is Anthropic's guide, copied into our check.
Based on (measured): wc on claude-settings CLAUDE.md at main 88266e82: 108 lines, 25,354 bytes, 19 lines over 300 characters.
Departs from: lint/check_claude_md_size.py, which warns on a fixed 200-line count — the check judges content (a line that restates a parent rule, or matters only under one folder) and cites the docs' figure as a pointer, not a gate.

lastAnswer.note: Owner in chat 19:25 CST: "yeah approved". Built by workflow claude-md-content-check; ruling lands in decision claude-md-shrink on that branch.

options.gain: No number of yours to defend; long lines cannot hide bloat.
options.how: The coordinator's planned check flags a child CLAUDE.md line that restates a parent rule or names only one folder; the size warning stays warn-only, counts bytes too, and links the docs' figure instead of owning a number.
options.label: Judge content, cite the docs' figure
options.lose: A content check is harder to build than a line count.

options.gain: Simple, and matches Anthropic's stated target.
options.label: Keep the 200-line warning
options.lose: Long lines pass it; our own file already does.

title: Should the CLAUDE.md size check stop counting lines and judge what each line is for?
why: The waste is restated and folder-only rules, which a line count cannot see.
